approach: Write the v-s line as an equation, use a = v dv/ds to get acceleration as a function of s, and read off its intercept and slope.

steps.text: Write the given straight-line v-s graph as an equation with a positive intercept c and a positive slope m.
Use the identity that relates acceleration to velocity and displacement.
The slope of the v-s line is constant, so dv/ds = m; substitute this and the expression for v.

This is again a straight line in s, with a positive intercept mc and a positive slope m², so the a-s graph is also a straight line with a positive intercept and a positive slope, matching the graph shown.
steps.equation: a-s line: intercept = mc, slope = m²

final_answer.value: a = mc + m²s, a straight line in s with positive intercept mc and positive slope m², matching the graph shown

common_mistakes.text: Using a = dv/dt directly with the v-s slope m as if it were a time rate gives a as a constant, missing that a depends on s through the v(dv/ds) relation.
